problem:
Which of the following are stochastic matrices?

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-0.1 & 0.2 \\ 1.1 & 0.8\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}0.1 & 0.2 \\ 0.9 & 0.8\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}0.5 & 0 & 0.5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0.5 & 0 & 0.5\end{aligned}]
$$

feedback.problem:
A certain company produces two types of footwear: casual and sports. The following table describes how the number of customers changes between both types of footwear each year:

|  |  | From: |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | **Casual** | **Sports** |
| To: | **Casual** | $0.55$ | $0.7$ |
| **Sports** | $0.45$ | $0.3$ |  |

That is, $45%$ of casual customers switch to sports each year, and $70%$ of sports customers change to casual.

Currently, $700\,000$ customers purchase casual footwear, while $300\,000$ customers purchase sports footwear. How many customers will purchase sports footwear in one year? You may assume that the total number of customers doesn't change.
feedback.worked_solution:
From the table, we can build the corresponding stochastic matrix: 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.55 & 0.7 \\ 0.45 & 0.3\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector describing the number of customers for each type of footwear is

$$
[\begin{aligned}700\,000 \\ 300\,000\end{aligned}].
$$

Dividing the vector above by the total number of customers $(1\,000\,000),$ we get the stochastic vector of the initial state:

$$
{x}_{0}=\frac{1}{1\,000\,000}[\begin{aligned}700\,000 \\ 300\,000\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0.7 \\ 0.3\end{aligned}]
$$

To find the state vector ${x}_{1}$ after one year, we apply one step of the Markov chain:

$$
{x}_{1}=P{x}_{0}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =P{x}_{0} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.55 & 0.7 \\ 0.45 & 0.3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0.7 \\ 0.3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.595 \\ 0.405\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, after one year, $40.5%$ of customers will purchase sports footwear. Computing $40.5%$ of $1\,000\,000,$ we obtain

$$
1\,000\,000\cdot 0.405=405\,000.
$$

Therefore, $405\,000$ customers will purchase sports footwear in one year.
